children: VME Companies, a provider of offshore EPC modules and separation technologies, filed an S-1 to go public. The Texas-based holding company plans to list on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the ticker “VME,” with Kingswood Capital Partners as the representative underwriter. Pricing, share count and offering size were not disclosed, and listing approval is pending.

VME Companies is a holding company that operates two primary businesses: EPC & Modular Solutions and Separation Technologies. The EPC & Modular Solutions segment designs and fabricates topside process modules and integrated systems for FPSOs and other offshore facilities, leveraging engineering and fabrication hubs across Southeast Asia. Its modular approach is intended to reduce offshore installation time and improve capital efficiency for customers.

The Separation Technologies segment, based in Tyler, Texas, supplies engineered oil, gas and water separation equipment, pressure vessels, internals, and packaged systems for both offshore and onshore applications. Across both segments, the company delivers project-based solutions without retaining ownership of completed assets, and serves international oil companies, national oil companies, FPSO operators, and EPC contractors.
: The global FPSO market is projected to reach about $33.91 billion by 2030, up from $24.52 billion in 2026.
: Forecast CAGR of roughly 8.5% through 2030 driven by deepwater developments and modernization.
: Specialist in FPSO topsides and modular fabrication with a Southeast Asia footprint.
: SBM Offshore, MODEC, Saipem, McDermott, Technip Energies, and regional fabrication yards.
: Cyclical activity, capacity constraints, execution certainty priorities, and rising safety/emissions requirements.
: Revenue concentration with Yinson Production entities and Santos-related entities totaled ~72.2% in 2025 and ~78.7% in 2024.
: Primary fabrication yard in Batam, Indonesia (≈28 hectares/74 acres) with a 185-meter jetty and 25,000–30,000 metric ton annual capacity.
: Engineering and fabrication in Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia; Separation Technologies in Tyler, Texas; global project deliveries.
: Licensed technologies from Dow DuPont (sulfate removal) and 3M (seawater deaeration).
: Backlog of approximately $127.1 million as of June 30, 2026.
: 2,000+ projects completed and modules supplied to 60+ FPSOs; TRIR of 0.14 across 2024–2025; workforce of 190 employees plus scalable contracted labor (up to ~6,500).
: Down 38% year over year for the six-month period (vs. $40.3 million in 1H 2025)
: ($0.59 million) net loss (six months ended June 30, 2026)

, Chief Executive Officer, President and Chairman - Over three decades in energy and process engineering; prior roles at Kvaerner Process Systems, Chicago Bridge & Iron, Cameron, and Chevron Phillips Chemical.

, Senior Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer (Director Nominee) - Leads EPC & Modular Systems operations and business development; prior roles at Kvaerner Process Systems Asia Pacific.
, Chief Financial Officer - 30+ years in accounting, finance, and capital markets; prior experience at Deloitte, U.S. Bancorp Investments, and other advisory roles; CPA.
, Vice President, Process Solutions - 24 years with VME; co-inventor on electrostatic coalescing technology; broad operational and commercial experience across process equipment.
, Vice President of Accounting - ~20 years with the company overseeing accounting, reporting, treasury, and internal controls.
, Director Nominee - Former Global CFO of Morrow Sodali; strategic finance advisor with CFO Consulting Partners.
: Working capital for project execution, targeted investments in engineering and infrastructure, repayment of approximately $5.0 million of debt, and general corporate purposes.
